body:
Hello!

Closes #34102

This adds an `nvim://` URI scheme for "Open in Editor" integration from external tools such as browsers, file managers, and error reporters.

### Format

```
nvim://open?file={path}[&line={n}][&column={n}][&server={addr}]
```

Only `open` is supported in this PR. The parser keeps an `action` field so the URI shape can be extended later, but the current behavior is intentionally limited to opening a file.

### Behavior

1. The URI is parsed as an open-file request with optional `line`, `column`, and `server`
2. If `&server={addr}` is provided, Nvim connects to that specific instance
3. Otherwise, Nvim auto-discovers existing instances via socket files in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`
4. If a server is found, the file is opened there and the new process exits
5. If no server is found, the file is opened locally

Files opened via `nvim://open?...` are handled by `vim.ui.edit()`, so users can customize how the file opens inside Nvim.

Example override:

```lua
vim.ui.edit = function(path, opts)
  vim.cmd.tabedit(path)
  if opts and opts.line then
    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { opts.line, (opts.column or 1) - 1 })
  end
end
```

### Setup

This reuses the existing `nvim.desktop` file. Users can register Nvim as the handler for `nvim://` URIs:

```bash
xdg-mime default nvim.desktop x-scheme-handler/nvim
```

The desktop entry is updated to use `%U` so URI arguments are passed through correctly.

Thanks!

comment_data.body:
can `vim.ui.open()` handle this? we should not need another hook point. users/plugins can override `vim.ui.open` if they want. LMK if I'm missing something.

if `vim.ui.open()` isn't the right "layer", then maybe it's time to introduce `vim.ui.edit()` (name/module TBD). It will handle `nvim://`, and later, will fill the role of `gf`, and even `:edit` could delegate to it.

The main point is that hooks (aka "providers") are exposed as module functions, not global variables.

comment_data.body: I want `nvim://open?...` to be the canonical URI that external tools emit, so integrations do not all choose different command-specific forms. I removed the `g:uri_opencmd` hook and reworked this so `open` is customized through `vim.ui.edit()` instead. Explicit commands like `tabedit` and `split` are still supported for fixed behavior, but the docs now recommend `open` as the preferred integration form.

small suggestion, instead of outright rejecting the "open" cmd why not have it fallback to "edit" but allow the handling to be configurable, the option could be named something like `vim.uri.opencmd` and the changes could be something like

```diff
+vim.uri.opencmd = 'edit'

local nvim_uri_cmds = {
  drop = true,
  edit = true,
  split = true,
  tabedit = true,
  tabnew = true,
  vsplit = true,
+  open = true,
}
```

```diff
+    if cmd == 'open' then
+      cmd = vim.uri.opencmd
+    end
+
    return {
      cmd = cmd,
      file = params.file,
      line = tonumber(params.line),
      column = tonumber(params.column),
      server = params.server,
    }
  end
```

yes i know the suggested code is very naive and a check should be done to ensure that `vim.uri.opencmd` is a real valid command but at this suggestion level that's neither here nor there.
@justinmk should the lua logic for this be in `_core/`? I would think so but I'm not as knowledgeable about what should be placed there as you.

> I went ahead and added `file://` support as well.

So I didn't notice this before, but between 0.11 and master, support for `file://` was already added (e.g. `nvim file:///etc/motd` opens `/etc/motd`). I tried to `git bisect` this addition but the feature is old enough that I cannot compile Nvim that far back. What do the changes you made do to improve this feature from how it already exists?

@superatomic, nvim can only load `file://` uris via **netrw**, not natively. And if netrw is disabled then it doesn't work, you can try it for yourself:

```lua
-- minmal.lua
vim.g['loaded_netrw'] = 1 -- disable netrw
```
and then running the following command
```bash
nvim --clean -u minimal.lua file:///some/file
```
Got it! Thank you for clarifying. Interesting that this behavior of netrw was added recently.

@justinmk anything that needs to be done before this can be merged? I'd quite like `file://` support that this PR adds (and although I have less of a use for `nvim://`, it still seems like a good feature).

> why not have it fallback to "edit" but allow the handling to be configurable, the option could be named something like `vim.uri.opencmd`

Not in favor of any configuration for this initial phase. Feel free to make a feature request for that.
Yes sorry been busy---I'll try to get to it this week

I'm really excited about this feature but the URI spec warrants further discussion. 

I'm not currently in love with the URI spec because:

1. All neovim can do is "open" a file. I did some research into the spec - almost all of these other editors do not leverage other subcommands besides open. Would we either (I think it's redundant)? This is not actually a big deal for me but related to # 3.
2. There are _many_ ways to open a file in neovim; enumerating them in a root-level `{cmd}` makes me nervous. Instead, providing a way to hook into the uri open/take the action afterwards is more sustainable. I like the approach you suggested in the docs, overriding a function and running a custom command I think ought to SUPPLANT `{cmd}` entirely.
3. I'd like to reuse `file://` parsing code - and encoding must be carefully considered (filenames can contain `&`!). Something like `nvim://open?`, for example, which nests the `?file://` inside of the URI, makes this _really_ difficult. Broader refactoring may be due in uri code...
4. `&server=` should be in a follow-up.
5. Erroring and error recovery: what if the line is invalid? what if the column is invalid? I would like if this is more obviously pointed out in a) the pr desc and b) the docs
6. Testing: make sure the non-happy paths are testing, it's rather light 

What about something like this? (just off the top of my head, haven't given it too much thought):

```
nvim:///home/barrett/project/lua/foo%3fbar.lua?line=42&column=7&server=%2frun%2fuser%2f1000%2fnvim.123.0
``` 

Thanks so much for the PR, happy to help however.
@justinmk, sorry it's taken so long but I've cleaned up the code, reduced the scope, and fixed the ci :+1:
Where can we see the most updated description of what the code actually does now? For example, the PR description still mentions the user of `server=`. Could you update it with the latest changes?

The pr description is up-to-date. I purposefully left the optional `server` in:

Many tools allow you to customize the specific `Open File in` link, and the server provides a mechanism to target a specific neovim instance---if you consistently work in a particular project, then you can name that server instance. Without this, the only thing I can do is just default to the first available neovim instance which may not be the instance you want if you have different instances open in different projects

As Justin said earlier, less code = easier for us to review; it's not about whether or not it should be in the end product.  Importantly, the intermediate state of the nvim URI _not_ having a server is still valid.

> As Justin said earlier, less code = easier for us to review; it's not about whether or not it should be in the end product. Importantly, the intermediate state of the nvim URI not having a server is still valid.

I'm not sure I see the point in removing code that's already working---supporting a named server is as simple as the following:

```lua
local function find_server(server)
  if server then
    return connect(server)
  end
```

The complicated part is handling the case where there is no server given

I'll leave it up to @justinmk, but I strongly push to release this with the server option
@justinmk, do you have any more comments or is this good to go?
